subject: Commitment unit math & remedy ladder — packaging options for Dedicated GPU pools (Terrasight)
messages:
From: Kellen Park <kellen@terrasight.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@terrasight.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Dedicated GPU packaging and SLA remedies

Hi Priyom —

Thanks again for the demo on Friday. Our engineering and procurement teams are reviewing the Dedicated packaging and we have a couple of asks before we go to our buying committee:

- Can you confirm how a "Capacity Unit" maps to GPUs and vram for the reserve? Our workload is a mix of 8k token chains and interactive chat.
- We want to understand the throughput guarantee: is the guarantee expressed as tokens/sec per unit, or as sustained qps for a pinned GPU?
- On SLA remedies: the draft contract ties credits to "unavailable capacity" but doesn’t call out partial degradation (eg degraded throughput on burst traffic). We need clear remedy ladder: partial (<10%), moderate (10–40%), severe (>40%) throughput impacts.

Can you send a short note with the proposed definitions and a sample remedy ladder? Procurement would like that in writing so they can include it in the redlines.

Thanks —
Kellen
Sr. Platform PM, Terrasight

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kellen Park <kellen@terrasight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated GPU packaging and SLA remedies

Hi Kellen —

Appreciate the detailed asks — we've been discussing exactly this on our product side and I’ll summarize our recommended approach below. Attaching a short spreadsheet that maps Capacity Unit (CU) definitions to common GPU SKUs and a proposed remedy ladder PDF for procurement review.

Definitions (proposed):
- Capacity Unit (CU): a contractual unit representing a baseline of dedicated inference capacity, defined as the equivalent of 1x A100-80GB device for purposes of throughput and KV cache sizing. For lower-memory GPUs, a CU represents equivalent aggregate CUDA cores and memory via pooling (e.g., 2x A100-40GB ≈ 1 CU). See attached capacity_definitions_v2.xlsx for mapping.
- Throughput Guarantee: expressed as "sustained token-throughput per CU" and "burst qps per CU for 60-second windows." Contract language should include both: baseline sustained throughput (tokens/sec/CU) and burst (requests/sec/CU) with a defined measurement window.
- Degradation categories: Partial (<10% below baseline), Moderate (10–40%), Severe (>40%). Remedies trigger when measured sustained throughput falls into these bands for a 5-minute rolling window for Moderate/Severe; partial triggers require 30+ minute sustained deviation.

Remedy ladder (summary):
- Partial: 10% service credit of monthly commitment pro-rated to affected CU-hours.
- Moderate: 25% credit + remediation plan and priority engineering support.
- Severe: 50% credit + option for temporary additional CU at no charge until remediation completed.

Notes / caveats:
- Credits are computed per CU-hour impacted, not per-API call, to align with reserved capacity economics.
- We propose a definition for "affected CU-hours" that excludes scheduled maintenance windows and customer-caused overloads per section X.

I’m happy to walk procurement through these numbers. If this direction looks good I can surface redline language for the MSA and get Ben to prepare a discounted pricing matrix aligned to commitment tiers.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_definitions_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping CUs to GPU SKUs), Terrasight_Redlines_v3.pdf (proposed remedy ladder)

From: procurement@terrasight.com
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kellen Park <kellen@terrasight.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Terrasight redlines to Dedicated MSA (initial)

Priyom / Ben —

Please find initial procurement redlines attached (excerpted below). We appreciate the definitions but procurement needs explicit contract language. High level asks:

1) Replace the "equivalent of 1x A100-80GB" phrasing with an arithmetic definition: CU = (Sum of GPU vram in GB * GPU compute factor) / 80, where compute factor is specified per GPU SKU in Exhibit A.
2) Throughput measurement: require that Redwood publish a per-CU live metric for sustained token-throughput and an API for historical 5-minute windows.
3) Remedy ladder escalation: add a cap on cumulative credits at 100% of monthly commit per event and define a max annual cap.

Excerpt (procurement redline):
- Section 4.1: Definition of Capacity Unit — redlined to require numeric mapping and a table in Exhibit A.
- Section 5.3: SLA Credits — redlined to add caps and an alternate definition for measuring "affected CU-hours" that excludes bursts above Customer’s documented traffic profile.

We’ll attach the full redline PDF; please respond with trackable contract language and confirm whether Redwood can support a live metric feed (one-minute granularity preferred).

Thanks,
Terrasight Procurement

Attachment: Terrasight_MSA_Redlines_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Terrasight redlines to Dedicated MSA (initial)

Priyom / Laura —

Quick thoughts before I reply to procurement:

- The arithmetic definition procurement requests is fine, but Exhibit A needs to be fixed so it doesn’t force us to renegotiate every new GPU SKU. Propose we tie the compute factor to a published Redwood SKU table that we can version with 30 days' notice.
- Live metric feed: we can provide 1-minute aggregated metrics for throughput per reserved pool via our Console API; this is an ops-level capability we should offer as part of Dedicated Premium. Let's scope whether Terrasight wants it as part of the base commit or as an add-on.
- Credit caps: we can accept a per-event cap at 100% of monthly commit but push back on annual caps that would compound to zero economics. Instead propose an annual aggregate cap at 200% of monthly commit.

I’ll draft alternative contract language for section 4.1 and 5.3 and attach a sample Exhibit A that references a published SKU table. Priyom — want me to include a sample discount schedule tied to CU tiers (12, 36, 100 CU)?

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kellen Park <kellen@terrasight.com>, procurement@terrasight.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal: numeric CU definition, measurement and remedy ladder (Terrasight)

Kellen / Procurement team —

Following our internal sync, attached is our proposed contract language (Terrasight_Redlines_v3.pdf) and a compact Exhibit A (capacity_definitions_v2.xlsx) that solves for the SKU churn problem. High level summary of the changes in the draft:

1) Numeric CU definition: CU = floor((Sum(GPU_vram_GB * SKU_factor))/80). Exhibit A lists SKU_factor for common devices. The floor() preserves whole-CU accounting; partial CU consumption is billed as fractional CU-hours with clear rounding rules.

2) Measurement & telemetry: Redwood will expose a Console API endpoint (read-only) that returns per-pool 1-minute aggregated throughput and a historical 5-minute window dataset for the previous 30 days. We’ve proposed adding the live feed as part of Dedicated Premium.

3) Remedy ladder: we accepted procurement’s per-event cap at 100% of monthly commit. We counter-proposed the annual cap be 200% of monthly commit and added language for expedited remediation timelines and an option for temporary free CU replacement in Severe events.

Next steps: If this version is acceptable we can prepare a track-changes MSA for legal — I’d suggest a short call (30 minutes) to go over Exhibit A mechanics and the Dedicated Premium telemetry entitlement. I’m available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Terrasight_Redlines_v3.pdf, capacity_definitions_v2.xlsx
